video.title: If We Had to Make $1M Fast, We’d Start These Businesses

summary: Chris Koerner and fellow podcaster Nick trade ideas for reaching a $1M business in six months. They cover RV rentals, 30 AI wrappers in 30 days, offshore AI-native talent placement, AI cost-savings audits for large corporations, rolling up dormant newsletters, a 'hero workflow' AI automation agency (Chris built a GoHighLevel after-hours voice agent for garage door firms and got a yes in 57 minutes), liquidation flipping, buying a business to add AI value, glamping, HVAC coil cleaning, Bingo Loco-style events and a mowing fantasy camp. Final picks: buy a business plus AI, liquidation, RV rentals, and AI automation for small businesses. Key takeaway: pick one high-impact plug-and-play workflow per niche, validate demand with data before buying assets.

ideas.name: Dormant newsletter roll-up
ideas.one_liner: Buy burned-out small newsletters (3k-30k subs) in a niche cheaply or on contingency, aggregate them, sell CPM ads, and possibly go daily.

pricing.notes: 10k subs x 50% opens x $30 CPM = $150/send = $600/month weekly. Buy at 10c/sub now, $1/sub later; or seller finance/contingency.

acquisition_channels.details: Find dormant newsletters via Beehiiv/Kit/Substack public directories using AI agents (ChatGPT agent, Manus, Comet)

acquisition.how: Directory scraping and B2B outreach to newsletter owners automatable.

ideas.name: Hero-workflow AI automation agency (e.g. after-hours AI receptionist for garage door companies)

ideas.business_model: Setup fee + monthly retainer; alternatively pay only per closed lead
ideas.customer: Small home service businesses (garage door repair: $500-$3,000 jobs) that miss after-hours calls
ideas.problem: Missed and after-hours calls lose leads; owners overwhelmed by AI
ideas.offer: Plug-and-play AI voice agent/answering service built in GoHighLevel AI Employee

pricing.notes: Chris offered pay only when a lead closes.

tactics.name: Validate rental demand by scraping occupancy
steps: Search RVshare/Outdoorsy (or Airbnb glamping) for this weekend and a year out
Log availability by type in a spreadsheet
Buy the type/market with highest occupancy

tactics.name: Hero workflow selection
steps: Pain: clear operational cost/stress
Access: who can you reach
Infrastructure: uses some digital tools, not too many
Dollar savings: real savings
Pick high-impact, low-complexity, magic-feeling workflows; one per niche

quote.text: you're looking for hero workflows. And these are what hero workflows are. They're high impact and they're low complexity
quote.speaker: Nick

tactics.name: Live AI receptionist demo outreach
steps: Build GoHighLevel AI voice agent with ChatGPT knowledge base
Pick an un-saturated higher-ticket niche with after-hours calls (garage doors)
Scrape every company in the metro, randomise
Message offer: pay only when a lead closes

tactics.name: Dormant newsletter sourcing
steps: Use AI agents to list newsletters on Beehiiv/Kit/Substack directories with no send in a month
Offer pennies per subscriber or contingency/seller finance
Aggregate in one niche; sell CPM ads; convert weekly to daily

tactics.name: Lease with option to validate land businesses
steps: Lease raw land (e.g. $3k/month) with option to buy in a year
Install business (storage, glamping)
Buy only after validation

tactics.name: Pre-sell events with ads
steps: Run targeted ads for an event before buying gear
Refund if not enough tickets

warnings.warning: Self-managing a single rental asset has no scale and becomes annoying.

quote.text: You should never own a rental home unless you're going to own like 10, 20, hundred of them
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: The last 10% of vibe-coded apps is still the hardest part.
Companies get squeamish about percentage-of-savings pricing; prefer predictable fees.
Always 'just a few more months' of grinding can become permanent.
Plumbing/HVAC/electrical are saturated with PE and existing AI answering.

lessons.lesson: Validate rental demand with marketplace data before buying assets.
Learn by building first, then research and market.

quote.text: I just feel like you're only going to learn how to do it by building
quote.speaker: Nick

lessons.lesson: Piggyback on people who already have customer networks.
Large companies waste huge sums on manual processes; domain experts can find them.
Most small businesses don't answer after-hours calls; AI receptionists are a blue ocean.

quote.text: They're definitely not answering after 5:00 p.m. I just think that is a blue ocean
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Unbundle a pain point big companies hate doing (coil cleaning, stump grinding).

quote.text: Find the painoint that nobody really wants to do but they have to do and unbundle it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Packaging can turn a boring activity into a premium experience.
Equity for value-add can beat agency fees when you can't afford to buy.
Short focused intense build periods can buy long-term freedom.

evidence_quality.rationale: Brainstorm with mostly hypothetical numbers; some first-hand experience (RV rental, garage door outreach).
